prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules induce proximity between ubiquitin ligases and chosen proteins so that the cell removes them

statement.case_for: I have moved from my round-1 two-part configuration to B066 alone. Targeted protein degradation is a physical-chemical idea as much as a pharmacological one: a small molecule acts as an adaptor that holds two proteins together, and degradation efficiency is governed by ternary-complex cooperativity, residence time and surface complementarity, not by occupancy of an active site. That is induced proximity, a general principle of molecular organisation of the kind I value, and it is independently reproduced, with ternary-complex structures and degradation kinetics from many groups. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target gives the molecular-glue strand its mechanism, so the three names cover both strands under one citation. It is also the only candidate that a plurality of members already places first and that most members accept at least as an alternative.
statement.case_against: No degrader drug is approved, so we would recognise a mechanism and a platform ahead of the clinical verdict, and several colleagues think this may be one or a few years early. Ciulli (VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures, which are the physical-chemistry core), Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are left out, and Handa anchors the glue strand rather than the PROTAC concept, so the citation risks looking like two achievements. My own earlier parts are not refuted: phase separation remains the least settled on physiological relevance, and a single-name lipid nanoparticle award still leaves Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer out. Also, a drop of soft-matter and biophysical themes from the prize is a real cost I accept.

responses.point: You rank mechanistic confirmation above breadth of conceptual influence and note that degraders have ternary-complex structures even without an approved drug.
responses.response: This is the argument that moved me most. I answered Brzezinski's question about artefacts in round 1 by saying the concept of demixing is secure, but you are right that for the committee the relevant test is whether the molecular mechanism holds under careful measurement in many hands, and degraders pass it more cleanly than condensates in cells. I do not fully share your timing worry, because the mechanism rather than the drug is what we would credit, but I accept that it is a real risk.

responses.point: You concede that Handa's cereblon work is closer to a molecular-glue story than to the PROTAC concept, and that you have not resolved whether Ciulli should replace Handa.
responses.response: I would keep Handa. Cereblon as the target of thalidomide is the discovery that explains why glues work and shows that degradation can be achieved with a small molecule that was discovered rather than designed, which makes the single citation about induced proximity and not only about PROTACs. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are the strongest claim on the other side and the one that most appeals to me as a physical chemist, but a three-name cap forces a choice, and I would rather name the concept and the mechanism of the glues than the later enabling chemistry. I would not oppose Ciulli replacing Handa if the committee prefers PROTAC-centred credit.

responses.point: You hold B038 first for its clean attribution, and you note that a second prize on the Pd catalyst family might leave soft-matter and biophysical themes unrepresented.
responses.response: Thank you for the second point; I am not asking for representation as a criterion and I do not treat it as a substitute for scientific judgment. On the science, I accept that the attribution for Buchwald and Hartwig is the cleanest and maturity is not in doubt. My hesitation is the one you raise: the 2010 prize already honoured Pd cross-coupling as a strategy, and I still cannot say what C-N coupling enabled that the 2010 laureates did not. If B066 cannot reach five votes I could support B038, but I would need that question answered in the citation.

responses.point: You ask which specific condensate claims I regard as artefactual before accepting that phase separation is too early.
responses.response: Fair challenge. The concerns are about overexpressed constructs and optogenetic or concentrated in vitro droplets that do not form at endogenous levels, and about assays such as 1,6-hexanediol that perturb more than condensates. I do not claim the P-granule result is among them, but I accept that the committee cannot separate the established physics from the contested biology without more evidence than we have, so I no longer lead with B036 and keep it as an alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept recognition ahead of the first approved degrader, and what evidence short of approval is enough.
Whether Handa or Ciulli should hold the third place.
Whether a single-topic B066 prize can reach five votes when B038 and B057 each have a firm supporting bloc.
Whether the 2023 Medicine prize on mRNA modification weakens the delivery-chemistry alternative B015.
statement.conflict_note: No change. Lipid self-assembly is my own research field, so I am professionally close to the B015 and B036 literature, and I sit with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, but I have no personal or institutional tie to any named candidate that requires recusal, including those in B066.
